decision: Add stacks/ between live roots and reusable core modules
why: Stacks commonly reuse one core module for different purposes; bootstrap and storage modules were near copies per cloud
evidence: diff modules/<cloud>/bootstrap/state vs storage/bucket: 7, 9, 4 differing lines for aws, azure, gcp

decision: Keep legacy migration blocks and add stack-level moves
why: The operator applied deployments with the pre-native shared stacks/ layout
evidence: operator answer; old managed addresses identical across 1715e72..657f324

decision: Always enable prevent_destroy in core data-store modules
why: prevent_destroy must be a literal, so one policy applies to every stack; operator chose always on
result: AWS and GCP workload storage gain deletion protection

decision: Build a static address-continuity check before restructuring
why: A missed move would destroy and recreate real infrastructure; cloud plans need credentials
result: 10 stacks and 34 legacy addresses traced for 30 roots; removed and duplicate moves rejected

decision: Move compositions from modules/<cloud>/<group>/<stack> to stacks/ as a pure move before extracting core modules
why: A path-only change is reviewable alone and lands the stacks-layer tooling before any address changes
evidence: scratch lever compared tools/addresses.managed_addresses and tofu test -verbose plans for 30 roots at 2b88dcc and after the move; a local root applied at 2b88dcc planned no changes after tofu init
result: 0 address differences and 0 plan differences in 30 roots; existing working directories need tofu init (Module not installed until then)

decision: Extract the local catalog into modules/local/catalog with a stack-level moved block before any cloud core module
why: The chained move old -> module.stack.X -> module.stack.module.<core>.X needed proof with real OpenTofu, and only the local catalog applies without a cloud account
evidence: tools/migration_smoke.py applies tests/fixtures/legacy-local for dev and prod; prod is first moved to module.stack.terraform_data.catalog with tofu state mv
result: dev plans terraform_data.catalog and prod plans module.stack.terraform_data.catalog as previous_address of module.stack.module.catalog.terraform_data.catalog; both no-op with unchanged IDs and outputs

decision: Extract modules/azure/storage-account and modules/azure/network; keep each resource group in its stack
why: Bootstrap and storage stacks duplicated the account, container, and name formula; resource groups differ in prevent_destroy, so they stay as stack glue
evidence: tests/test_azure_core.py; scratch lever compared tofu test -verbose plans for 9 Azure roots at origin/refactor/local-catalog-core and after with addresses rewritten by the move map; removing any of the 8 stack moves fails tools/check_layout.py
result: 0 differing plan lines in 9 roots after address rewrite; 8 moves, 2 core modules; no prevent_destroy change because both Azure storage stacks already protected the account and container

decision: Extract modules/aws/kms-key, modules/aws/s3-bucket, and modules/aws/vpc; both AWS bucket stacks call the key and bucket modules
why: The bootstrap and storage stacks duplicated the bucket, its settings, and the key; the S3 naming rule belongs in one module
evidence: scratch lever rewrote addresses with the 17-entry move map and diffed tofu test -verbose plans for the 9 AWS roots at the base and after; check_layout rejected each of the 17 stack moves when removed alone
result: 0 differing plan lines in 9 roots (base runs repeat byte for byte); every removal named its legacy address; storage bucket gains prevent_destroy
